clue.text: Excuse certain to give rise to amusement

parts.note: a plea is an excuse offered in defence
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A pretext that is bound to raise a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is enjoyment or delight, a close synonym of this word.

clue.text: Getting a page to awaken a writer

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
to roust is to rouse or awaken

explanation.surface: Sending a boy servant to wake up an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was a French novelist, author of In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: The viewer's screen

parts.note: the viewer is the organ of sight, and its screen is the fold of skin that shields it

explanation.surface: A television watcher's set.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin covering the eye acts as its protective shutter.

clue.text: Gathering coal is gregarious

explanation.surface: Collecting coal is a sociable activity.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a party; as an adjective it means enjoying others' company.

clue.text: Serving men lie in because it makes for a speedy recovery

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers in service

indicators.note: in places the word lie inside the word for because

parts.note: since means because
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers sleep late since it helps them bounce back quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie in' looks like a lazy morning, but 'in' is a container signal; the Royal Engineers are a British army corps, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilience is the capacity to bounce back quickly from difficulty.

clue.text: The individual joining in to appease a merchant-banker

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words appease a merchant-banker, signalled by in

explanation.surface: Someone joins a deal to keep a merchant banker happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in the run 'appeaSE A MERchant'. 'The individual joining' describes one who joins things with seams.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sews seams is a person who joins pieces of fabric together.

clue.text: Rues time frittered in honourable retirement

indicators.note: frittered means broken into bits, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A retired person regrets the time wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor retired with an honorary title kept.

clue.text: Claim for finance

explanation.surface: Applying for funding.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert that something is true, or to keep someone supported financially.

clue.text: Turning a gun on the heartless guide

indicators.note: turning tells us the word for gun is reversed

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word the is dropped

explanation.surface: Pointing a gun at someone ruthless to direct him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses LUGER to REGUL; 'heartless' takes H from THE, giving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate is to control or steer, guiding how something runs.

clue.text: Being above those playing can be dull

parts.note: over means above
the cast are the actors playing in a show

explanation.surface: Being placed above the performers can be a dreary experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey, cloudy sky is dull.

clue.text: Cutting the guy taking flight

parts.note: he refers to a man, any guy
a wing gives flight; also a flight is a wing of a building or air force unit

explanation.surface: Someone is slashing at a man who is trying to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' joins the pieces: HE takes WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewing is chopping with an axe, a form of cutting wood or stone.

clue.text: The man without money and help going round in circles

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the man goes round the money

parts.note: sir is the form of address for a man
P for penny, a small amount of money
to ally is to join with and help

explanation.surface: A man left penniless and alone, getting nowhere fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: SIR goes round P (penny).
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving in a spiral way keeps turning around a centre.

clue.text: A Greek character much backed-Falstaff's companion

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: backed indicates the word for much is written in reverse order

parts.note: lots means much

explanation.surface: A Greek with plenty of support sides with the Shakespearean knight.
explanation.walkthrough: PISTOL is one of Falstaff's cronies in Shakespeare's Henry plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistol is a swaggering ensign who follows Sir John in Shakespeare's history plays.

clue.text: Underworld bigwig offering deal

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
a tribute is an offering

explanation.surface: A gangster boss with a proposed bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bigwig' suggests a mob boss, but DIS is the Roman god ruling the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal cards is to hand them out to players.

clue.text: Stir up iced cocktail for a professional person

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mix up an iced drink for a guest in professional circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiropodist who treats feet is a trained professional.

clue.text: Works of new poets are ordered

indicators.note: ordered says the pooled letters with are are put into another order
new poets suggests a fresh batch of writers, but it signals the word poets is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: New poets' collected works are put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' reads like an adjective for the poets and 'ordered' like a verb, but both signal rearrangement: the letters of POETS and ARE together are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Operates and works both mean functions or runs.

clue.text: Sort of teasing only youngsters find agreeable?

definitions.text: Sort of teasing only youngsters find agreeable?

parts.words: Sort of teasing only youngsters find agreeable?
parts.note: split it into three short words: something unpleasant once you are older, so only the young like it

explanation.surface: A kind of mockery that only children enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful banter or light teasing.

clue.text: Walking free in some discomfort

indicators.note: in places the word for free inside the word for discomfort

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain, some discomfort
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Walking about freely despite some pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Striding is walking with long steps.

clue.text: Yielding to pressure, so sanctimonious about final urban development

indicators.note: about tells us the word for sanctimonious goes around the word for final

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
last means final
a city is a large urban development

explanation.surface: Giving in under pressure, a self-righteous planner reviews the last stage of town growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal here, not 'concerning'; PI as slang for pious is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasticity is the property of a material that changes shape under stress.

clue.text: Shout out in pain being cowardly

parts.note: to yell is to shout out
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Crying out in pain shows a lack of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for lacking courage.

clue.text: Aim straight

explanation.surface: Point straight ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means point at a target; as an adjective it means without detour.

clue.text: A shooting star of remote origin

definitions.text: A shooting star of remote origin

parts.words: A shooting star of remote origin
parts.note: a streak in the night sky from space, not a celebrity marksman from far away

explanation.surface: A celebrity marksman from a faraway place.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a space rock burning up in the atmosphere, coming from far off.

clue.text: Fruit for when one's in the shower

indicators.note: in places the word for one's within the word for shower

parts.note: rain is a shower
I'S is one is, giving IS

explanation.surface: A snack to eat while standing under the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is 'I is', so IS goes into RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Salvation is seen by the fortune-teller

definitions.meaning: a rope or means of rescue in a crisis
a palm reader studies the crease on the hand said to show length of years

explanation.surface: A palmist foresees someone's rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a rescue rope and the palm crease read by palmists bear this name.

clue.text: An American soldier in the cart turned very sad

indicators.note: in places the soldier within the reversed vehicle
turned means the word cart is read backwards

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US soldier's cart overturned, which is terrible news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses CART to TRAC, and GI goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic causes great sorrow, deeply sad.

clue.text: Bovine look that's really sweet

definitions.meaning: the gaze of a male cow
a hard peppermint-flavoured British boiled sweet

explanation.surface: A cow's gaze that is truly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: A BULLSEYE is a traditional British boiled sweet, striped black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull's eye is a bovine organ of sight; the name is also a classic striped mint candy.

clue.text: Express despair about the French transport in winter

indicators.note: about tells us the word for despairing goes around the French article

parts.note: to sigh is to express despair
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Despairing of a Frenchman's choice of winter travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge pulled over snow is a vehicle used in winter.

clue.text: Abnormally wet areas in the main

indicators.note: abnormally signals the letters are in an irregular arrangement

explanation.surface: Damp patches turning up in odd places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic name for the open ocean; 'Abnormally' rearranges WET AREAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is the high sea, made of salty ocean liquid.
